data.body:
FIXED (rebar-debug protocol, worktree `fix/7a79-cache-floor`) — the floor gate is in, with the
genuine detection preserved and the constant single-sourced.

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed, not read off source)

`warn_if_cache_ineffective`'s predicate had an UPPER-open lower bound only: `input_tokens > 0`.
A live probe drove the function with the exact per-call `input_tokens` values recorded in this
ticket (1822, 2184, 2317, 3140) plus 8192, all with zero/zero counters and
`caching_requested=True`. Every one emitted the identical warning — the 8192 (cacheable) case
and the four sub-floor (never-cacheable) cases were INDISTINGUISHABLE in the log. That is the
mechanism: the predicate cannot separate "a cacheable prompt silently failed to cache" (real,
actionable) from "the prompt was never cacheable" (expected, unactionable).

Legitimacy = `defect`, cited against the codebase's OWN design invariant: `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`
(pass1.py) already documents that a sub-floor prefix "never caches" and already suppresses cache
WARM-UP below it. The warning path simply never consulted the fact the warm-up path relies on.

## The fix

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — NEW shared home for `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096`, sited
  next to `cache_settings_for`: the module that already owns prompt-cache knowledge, and the
  lowest layer BOTH consumers already sit above. (The plan's first-named candidate; `config.py`
  would have made a per-model cache fact look like an operator knob.)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the literal becomes
  `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. The name and both historical
  call sites (:222, :496) are untouched. No cycle: `capabilities` imports only stdlib at module
  top. ONE definition, per the AC — no second literal, no hand-sync (unlike `DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`).
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — `input_tokens > 0` becomes
  `input_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. Signature UNCHANGED, so `runner.py:509` needed no
  edit (that file is owned by a parallel session).

Deliberately NOT done: the ticket's secondary suggestion to aggregate per-RUN instead of per-CALL.
The floor alone reduces the ~20 lines/run to zero when caching works, and a per-run aggregate is a
larger design change touching `usage_log`/`runner` (both owned by parallel sessions). Worth a
follow-up ticket only if per-call lines still prove noisy above the floor.

## RED confirmed first, and the test has teeth

NEW `tests/unit/test_cache_floor_warning.py` (11 cases). Pre-fix: 6 failed / 5 passed —
the 5 sub-floor cases failed on the intended assertion with the captured warning in the pytest
log (right reason, not an import/fixture error), and the single-source case failed with
`AttributeError: module 'rebar.llm.capabilities' has no attribute 'CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS'`
(also the right reason). Critically, the 4 above-floor cases and the "other silence reasons" case
were GREEN pre-fix and stayed green — that is the standing proof the genuine detection was never
weakened, only bounded.

Post-fix 11/11 green. Mutation check: re-seeding the exact root cause (`>= FLOOR` back to `> 0`)
returned the suite to 5 failed, then restored. The test is not a tautology.

The floor is imported FROM `pass1` in the test rather than restated as `4096`, so if the two
definitions ever drift apart again the boundary cases fail on their own.

## One pre-existing test had a real behavioral dependency — flagged, not silently bent

`tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py::test_warns_when_caching_was_requested_but_both_counters_are_zero`
pinned `input_tokens=4029` — which is itself BELOW the 4096 floor, so it went red on the fix. Raised
that one literal to 40290 (a realistic gate-prompt size); every assertion is intact
(`len(warnings) == 1`, model-name-in-message) and the docstring now says why a cacheable size is
required. A literal-for-literal expectation change, not a weakened test.

HONEST CONSEQUENCE, worth recording: the originally MEASURED opus-4-5 defect was observed at 4029
input tokens, i.e. sub-floor. Under the new contract that specific reading is classified as
expected rather than a defect. This is the correct call — 4029 tokens genuinely cannot cache, so
zero/zero there was never evidence of anything — but it does mean the narrowest form of the
original observation no longer trips the warning. The defect CLASS (a cacheable prompt that does
not cache) remains fully caught, which is the signal that has operator-actionable value.

## Gates

`make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0 (407 files). 576 passed across
`test_bedrock_provider` / `test_structured_run_seam` / `tests/unit/workflow/` /
`test_prompt_cache_split` / the new file; full `tests/unit` sweep run separately. Module-size cap
respected — largest touched file is `pass1.py` at 735 of 800.

Sibling sweep (root cause as a CLASS: a cache predicate reading zero counters as a defect without
a cacheability bound): every other `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` site in `src/` only
aggregates or reports the counters (`usage_log`, `sizing`, `voter`, `finalize`,
`runner.py:557` INFO line) — none interprets zero as a defect. No siblings.

## Replication

Driving the function exactly as `runner.py:509` does, with all five live-observed sub-floor
readings: zero warnings emitted. The above-floor zero/zero case: one warning, naming the model.
The original report no longer reproduces.

## Remaining AC (needs an operator, cannot be self-attested)

`[operator-attested]` a full `rebar review-plan` run emitting zero cache warnings while its
aggregate `cache_write_tokens > 0`. Unit-level evidence is complete; the live run needs real
provider credentials and a human attestation.

Not pushed — the orchestrator cherry-picks this onto the Gerrit stack.
